M1-INSERT: Registers a new student (Tanvi) using the procedure pkg_timebank.enrol_student.
One transaction does 2 writes: the STUDENT row + a starter GRANT of 3 credits in CREDIT_TXN.
So a student can never exist without credits (TOTAL participation in 'posts').
Her 2 phone numbers go into STUDENT_PHONE: PhoneNo is a MULTIVALUED attribute -> own table.
M1-UPDATE: Closes Sara's account by setting account_status = 'INACTIVE' (a SOFT delete), then restores it.
Why not DELETE? BOOKING and CREDIT_TXN reference STUDENT with no ON DELETE clause,
so Oracle would block the delete to protect session history and the ledger.
M1-DELETE: Deletes one of Aarav's two phone numbers.
This is a safe, real DELETE: STUDENT_PHONE came from a multivalued attribute and no table references it.
M1-Q1: AGE is a DERIVED attribute - it is NOT stored. It is calculated from DOB:
M1-Q2: *** MOST IMPORTANT QUERY OF MEMBER 1 *** - a 4-table JOIN with two LEFT JOINs.
It labels every student: TUTOR ONLY / TUTEE ONLY / BOTH / NEITHER YET.
BOTH (Kabir, Arjun) proves the specialization is OVERLAPPING.
NEITHER YET (Sara) proves it is PARTIAL. So we used mapping option 8A (superclass + subclass tables).
LEFT JOIN is required - an INNER JOIN would hide students missing from a subclass.
M1-Q3: NESTED (non-correlated) subquery: students whose balance is below the campus average.
The inner subquery does not use the outer row, so Oracle runs it only ONCE.
M1-Q4: CORRELATED subquery: joined more than 30 days ago but never booked a session.
NOT EXISTS uses s.student_id from the outer query, so it is re-run for EVERY outer row.
M1-Q5: AGGREGATE with GROUP BY and HAVING: a department scoreboard.
WHERE filters ROWS before grouping; HAVING filters GROUPS after grouping (it can use COUNT).
M1-Q6: ANALYTIC (window) functions: rank students by credit balance inside their department.
RANK, DENSE_RANK, PERCENT_RANK, NTILE, LAG with PARTITION BY department.
Unlike GROUP BY, window functions keep EVERY row and add the rank beside it.
M2-INSERT: Meera becomes a tutor: insert into TUTOR, then TUTOR_SKILL, then 2 SLOT rows.
The order is forced by foreign keys (a TUTOR must exist before its skills and slots).
Meera was already a tutee - now she is in BOTH subclasses (overlapping).
Her slot_no starts again at 1: slot_no is the PARTIAL KEY of the WEAK entity SLOT.
M2-UPDATE: Promotes a tutor to EXPERT in a subject if they have >= 2 completed sessions in it
AND an average rating >= 4.0. Uses two CORRELATED subqueries inside the WHERE clause.
Only ratings written by the TUTEE are counted (a booking has two reviews, one from each side).
'0 rows updated' is a correct result on this data: nobody has met the bar yet.
M2-DELETE: Removes a slot Neel no longer offers (his Saturday slot).
The NOT EXISTS guard checks no booking uses it - otherwise the COMPOSITE foreign key
(tutor_id, slot_no) from BOOKING would raise ORA-02292 'child record found'.
M2-Q1: SIMPLE query: the subject catalogue with the department that owns each subject.
M2-Q2: 5-table JOIN: the skill matrix - which tutor can teach which subject.
TUTOR_SKILL is the table made from the M:N relationship 'offers' (it has its own attributes).
DEPARTMENT is joined TWICE with different aliases (tutor's dept and subject's dept).
Shows CROSS-DEPARTMENT tutoring: Rohan is Mechanical but teaches Database Systems.
M2-Q3: NESTED subquery with NOT IN: subjects that nobody teaches (coverage gaps).
This is the PARTIAL participation of SUBJECT in 'offers'.
NOT IN is safe only because tutor_skill.subject_id is NOT NULL (one NULL would return no rows).
M2-Q4: CORRELATED subquery: published slots that nobody has booked for next week.
The NOT EXISTS correlates on THREE things: tutor_id, slot_no and the computed date.
M2-Q5: AGGREGATE with GROUP BY / HAVING: teaching capacity vs demand per subject.
COUNT(DISTINCT tutor_id) avoids counting the same tutor twice.
M2-Q6: ANALYTIC functions: rank tutors inside each subject (best first).
RANK, COUNT() OVER, LAG and FIRST_VALUE with PARTITION BY subject.
M3-INSERT: Sara (who was in NEITHER subclass) becomes a TUTEE, then books Kabir's Friday slot.
1 lock the slot row (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE)  2 check it is free  3 check the pair weekly cap
4 INSERT the booking  5 move credits to escrow (HOLD -1.5 in the ledger).
Triggers check the overdraft floor and the slot time; the composite FKs check slot+subject belong to the tutor.
Note the SESSION CODE printed - only the tutee gets it.
M3-UPDATE: Reschedules the earliest upcoming booking by one week.
A correlated NOT EXISTS makes sure the new date is free, so rescheduling cannot double-book.
M3-DELETE: Purges old REQUESTED bookings that have no ledger rows.
'0 rows deleted' is correct here. CONFIRMED/COMPLETED bookings can NEVER be deleted
because CREDIT_TXN references them - deleting would orphan money.
M3-Q1: Start time is stored as decimal hours (16.5 = 16:30); dividing by 24 turns it into a clock time.
M3-Q2: 6-table JOIN: the complete session sheet (tutee, tutor, subject, slot, status).
Every join rebuilds one ER relationship from its foreign key.
The SLOT join uses BOTH tutor_id AND slot_no because SLOT is a weak entity (composite key).
M3-Q3: NESTED subquery with NOT IN: tutors with a completely free diary next week.
M3-Q4: CORRELATED subquery: tutors busier than the average tutor.
This one statement contains BOTH kinds: the correlated one (uses t.student_id, runs per tutor)
and a non-correlated one (campus average, runs once).
M3-Q5: AGGREGATE with GROUP BY / HAVING: booking funnel per subject.
SUM(CASE WHEN ... THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = conditional aggregation (pivots status into columns).
M3-Q6: ANALYTIC functions: each tutor's sessions with a RUNNING TOTAL of hours.
SUM() OVER (... ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW), ROW_NUMBER, RATIO_TO_REPORT.
GROUP BY would give only the total; window functions show total AND each session.
M4-INSERT: Inserts a goodwill GRANT of +1 credit for Ananya directly into the ledger.
balance_snapshot is computed inside the same statement (balance before + amount).
booking_id is NULL - it is the ONLY nullable foreign key in the schema
(partial participation of CREDIT_TXN in 'generates': grants have no session).
M4-UPDATE: Tightens the overdraft rule from -5 to -4 credits in CREDIT_POLICY, then restores it.
Rules live in a table (an index-organised table), so changing a rule needs no code change.
The trigger trg_credit_floor reads this value on every booking.
M4-DELETE: Clears stale escrow values on finished bookings (kept with COMMIT),
then DELETEs a policy row and immediately ROLLBACKs - showing a delete can be undone
M4-PROOF: *** SCREENSHOT THIS *** Two attempts to tamper with the ledger:
an UPDATE and a DELETE on CREDIT_TXN. Both MUST fail with ORA-20001.
The trigger trg_txn_immutable makes the ledger APPEND-ONLY (like real accounting).
M4-Q1: SIMPLE query: the passbook of student 102 (Diya), newest first.
GRANT +3, then HOLDs (negative) when she booked, RELEASE when a booking was cancelled.
M4-Q2: JOIN with LEFT OUTER JOIN: each ledger row with the session that caused it.
Must be OUTER: booking_id is NULL for GRANT/PENALTY rows, an INNER join would drop them.
M4-Q3: NESTED subquery in the FROM clause (inline view): net givers vs net takers.
The inner query totals the ledger per student; the outer query classifies them.
M4-Q4: CORRELATED subquery = TAMPER CHECK. Every snapshot must equal previous snapshot + amount.
EXPECTED RESULT: 'no rows selected'. No rows = the ledger has never been edited = PASS.
M4-Q5: *** THE CLOSED-ECONOMY AUDIT *** (most important query of the project)
First a GROUPING SETS summary per transaction type with a grand total,
then the equation:  all balances + escrow  =  grants - penalties.
VERDICT must say BALANCED (drift 0): no credits were created or lost.
M4-Q6: ANALYTIC functions: rebuild each student's running balance with SUM() OVER
and compare it with the stored balance_snapshot. Every row should say 'ok'.
M5-INSERT: (a) Adds the tutor review that one completed booking never got.
The trigger allows feedback only on COMPLETED sessions; the PK (booking_id, reviewer_role)
stops anyone reviewing the same session twice.
(b) Raises a dispute on the first CONFIRMED booking -> booking becomes DISPUTED, escrow is frozen.
dispute_no is a PARTIAL KEY (restarts at 1 for every booking) - DISPUTE is a weak entity.
M5-UPDATE: Triages disputes older than 2 days: status UNDER_REVIEW, assigned to the least-busy admin.
'0 rows updated' is correct now - the dispute was raised just a moment ago.
M5-DELETE: (a) Tutors retract their recent 4.0 reviews (written in the last 7 days, no dispute) - 3 rows.
Naming (booking_id, reviewer_role) identifies exactly one review - no extra review id needed.
(b) Deletes ratings from pairs who tutor each other (possible collusion).
0 rows in (b) is correct: our data has no colluding pairs.
M5-Q1: SIMPLE query with UNION ALL: reviews and disputes listed together.
UNION ALL (not UNION) because no duplicates are possible and it avoids a sort.
M5-Q2: SELF JOIN: FEEDBACK is joined to itself twice - once for the tutee's review, once for the tutor's.
Possible only because reviewer_role is part of the primary key.
OUTER joins, because many sessions have only one review or none.
M5-Q3: NESTED subquery, 3 levels: tutors rated above the campus average.
Campus average = average of each tutor's average (so busy tutors do not dominate).
M5-Q4: CORRELATED subquery: CREDIT-LOOP COLLUSION detector - two students who keep tutoring each other.
'no rows selected' = no suspicious pairs in our data (that is the good result).
A database cannot stop two people who agree to lie, but it can make the pattern visible.
M5-Q5: AGGREGATE with ROLLUP: rating distribution per subject plus an ALL SUBJECTS total row.
STDDEV shows the spread; GROUPING() detects the total row.
M5-Q6: ANALYTIC functions: is each tutor improving or slipping?
LAG (previous rating), moving average of last 3, DENSE_RANK and NTILE across campus.
A1: TCL demo: SAVEPOINT, ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT, and full ROLLBACK on Ishita's balance.
Add +2 goodwill, set a savepoint, add a wrong -2 penalty, ROLLBACK TO the savepoint:
only the penalty is undone. Then a full ROLLBACK undoes everything.
A2: ATOMICITY (the A in ACID): a booking that fails (tutor 101 has no slot 9)
leaves NO trace - the ledger row count is the same before and after.
PART B: CONCURRENCY demo is done separately with two windows:
then type COMMIT; in window 1 - window 2 fails with ORA-20005. Only one booking exists.
C1: EXPLAIN PLAN for 'find tutors of subject 101' - WITH the index.
Look for INDEX RANGE SCAN and note the COST.
C2: The same query with the /*+ FULL */ hint, which forces Oracle to ignore the index.
Look for TABLE ACCESS FULL and compare the COST with C1.
C3: Heuristic optimisation: selection is pushed down - FEEDBACK is filtered BEFORE the joins,
so fewer rows are joined. (Relational algebra is written in the file comments.)
C4: INDEX-ONLY scan: the answer comes from the index alone.
There is no TABLE ACCESS step - the table itself is never read.
PART D: Final closed-economy audit with pkg_timebank.audit_economy - must print BALANCED.
E1: Module 6: tutor leaderboard using a CTE (WITH clause) + DENSE_RANK, PERCENT_RANK, NTILE, LEAD.
E2: Module 6, GRAPH query without a graph database: CONNECT BY walks 'who learned from whom'.
Starts at Diya: she learned from Aarav (Aarav never booked anyone, so the chain ends there).
NOCYCLE stops infinite loops if two students taught each other (otherwise ORA-01436).
E3: ROLLUP: how much tutoring crosses department boundaries (with subtotals and grand total).
This is why DEPARTMENT is in the model at all.
